run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: Hotel Reservation
Namespace: hotel-reservation

A hotel reservation application built with Go and gRPC, providing backend in-memory and persistent databases, a recommender system for hotel recommendations, and a functionality to place reservations.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The hotel-reservation environment was built from scratch moments before the window closed: the monitoring stack (observe) came up 12:35–12:37 and all 20 hotel-reservation pods were created 12:37:39–12:37:54, so only about 30 s of application traffic exists at the window end (2026-11-21T12:38:12Z). In that window the application serves successfully: frontend returns HTTP 200 for /hotels, /recommendations and POST /reservation with millisecond latencies, the sampled traces carry no error status or error detail, and the rate service reports 569 received / 569 completed / 0 rejected / 0 expired. No alert rule is firing. The only fault-shaped state is fault-injection tooling: Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate were re-rolled at 12:37:41–12:37:43 (new ReplicaSets, same mongo:4.4.6 image) to mount ConfigMaps failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate at /scripts, and those ConfigMaps hold scripts that revoke the admin user's readWrite role on geo-db / rate-db or drop the admin user; no other mongo Deployment has such a mount. The declared fault was not seen to execute: MongoDB ACCESS logs show no shell login from 127.0.0.1 after each init script finished (last geo 12:37:45.734Z, rate 12:37:49.115Z), only geo/rate application connections follow, and no 'not authorized' line exists through 12:38:12Z. Two other anomalies were checked and are not tied to application impact: a ConfigMap stuck Terminating behind the cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup finalizer whose cleanup-controller is denied with HTTP 403 every ~2 s, and Prometheus failing to scrape search.hotel-reservation:9092 while the search gRPC service works. Because two equally implicated ConfigMaps exist and the injected fault itself was never observed, no single root-cause object is asserted.

claims.text: All 20 pods in namespace hotel-reservation were created between 12:37:39Z and 12:37:54Z; every pod is phase Running with all containers Ready and restartCount 0 (including rate-65d6967c95-ldz5q, search-567bb6c4b8-5cllx, geo-d4c78b89b-fgbgw and reservation-7d77c6cb59-65hwd), so the application had roughly 30 seconds of runtime before the window ended.

Namespace events for hotel-reservation begin only at 12:37:39Z: each Deployment shows one 'Scaled up replica set ... from 0 to 1' at 12:37:39–12:37:41, except mongodb-geo (old ReplicaSet mongodb-geo-78487c9767 scaled 1 to 0 at 12:37:41, new ReplicaSet mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8 created at 12:37:44) and mongodb-rate (mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf scaled 1 to 0 at 12:37:42, mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9 created at 12:37:44) — a second, configuration-only rollout of exactly these two workloads inside the incident window. The two FailedScheduling warnings refer to those replaced pods (mongodb-geo-78487c9767-45pfc, mongodb-rate-6747cb74bf-d2vdr) and are rollout artifacts.

Deployments mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate are at metadata.generation 2 and each mounts a configMap volume named 'failure-script' at /scripts sourced from ConfigMap failure-admin-geo and failure-admin-rate respectively (plus init-script volumes mongo-geo-script / mongo-rate-script at /docker-entrypoint-initdb.d); their running pods mongodb-geo-5ff578bcb8-42nq7 and mongodb-rate-56cc8659c9-cz8nw were created after that change, while mongodb-profile, mongodb-recommendation, mongodb-reservation and mongodb-user are at generation 1 with only a data volume.

ConfigMap failure-admin-rate contains revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh (db.revokeRolesFromUser('admin',[{role:'readWrite',db:'rate-db'}])), revoke-mitigate-admin-rate-mongo.sh which re-grants it, and remove-admin-mongo.sh (db.dropUser('admin')); ConfigMap failure-admin-geo contains the same set targeting geo-db. These are fault-injection and mitigation scripts, and no other object in the namespace references them.

The declared MongoDB privilege fault had not been executed by the window end: for 12:34:00–12:38:12Z Loki holds only 13 authentication lines for mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo — the four init-script shell authentications from 127.0.0.1 (geo admin 12:37:45.531Z, geo root 12:37:45.734Z, rate admin 12:37:48.928Z, rate root 12:37:49.115Z) and nine application authentications from pod IPs 10.244.234.152 (rate) and 10.244.7.207 (geo); no later localhost shell login — which a /scripts/revoke-admin-*.sh or remove-admin-mongo.sh run would produce — appears, and no 'not authorized' line is present.

After the two MongoDB pods were replaced, both dependent services initialised against their databases successfully: geo logged 'New session successfull...', 'Generating test data...', 'Successfull' and 'Successfully registered in consul' at 12:37:47Z, and rate logged the same sequence at 12:37:50Z followed by 'Read target port: 8084', 'Starting server...' and 'Successfully registered in consul'.

Application traces at the window end are successful: trace 065bf338048d3955 shows frontend 'HTTP GET /hotels' with http.status_code 200 in 6139 us and its fan-out (frontend -> search /search.Search/Nearby 2890 us -> search -> geo /geo.Geo/Nearby 49 us and rate /rate.Rate/GetRates 439 us -> memcached_get_multi_rate 336 us; reservation CheckAvailability 735 us; profile GetProfiles 1142 us), and trace 4367be0a702a20c1 shows 'HTTP POST /reservation' 200 in 11298 us with reservation MakeReservation 9601 us. None of the 80 longest spans read from the 314-row frontend sample carries an error status or error detail.

The rate service's own metrics at 12:38:12Z are error-free: rate_requests_received_total 569, rate_requests_completed_total 569, rate_requests_rejected_total 0, rate_requests_expired_total 0, rate_queue_depth 0 and rate_in_flight 0, with rate_backend_qps_limit 500 and rate_queue_capacity 256 (instance rate.hotel-reservation:9091).

Prometheus cannot scrape the search metrics endpoint: up{instance="search.hotel-reservation:9092",job="hotel-reservation-application"} is 0 at both sampled instants 12:37:12Z and 12:38:12Z, while up{instance="rate.hotel-reservation:9091"} is 1 at 12:38:12Z, and no search_* series (search_requests_total, search_rate_attempts_total / failures / successes / timeouts) exist in 11:38:12–12:38:12Z; the search gRPC port 8082 nevertheless serves spans. Service object 'search' declares ports 8082 and metrics 9092 matching the containerPorts.

The cleanup-controller pod cleanup-controller-785f8c5b5b-nlhmn logs 'cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden' every ~2 s from 12:37:59Z through 12:38:11Z, and ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token carries deletionTimestamp 2026-11-21T12:37:58Z with finalizer cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup, i.e. it is stuck Terminating; nothing mounts that ConfigMap and no application pod log references it.

kube-state-metrics has no hotel-reservation series at 12:38:12Z: kube_pod_info and kube_deployment_status_replicas_available only carry the namespaces kube-system, openebs, observe, local-path-storage and sregym, so kube_pod_owner / kube_replicaset_owner / kube_deployment_status_* cannot be evaluated for this app and the kube_*-based alert rules cannot see it.

Blackbox probe_success is 0 at 12:38:12Z for nearly every probed endpoint cluster-wide (hotel-reservation frontend:5000, profile:8081, rate:8084, recommendation:8085, user:8086, plus the astronomy-shop and social-network targets) while geo:8083, reservation:8087 and search:8082 are 1; because the failure spans unrelated namespaces it is not evidence of a hotel-reservation fault.

No alert was firing for this application: rule groups app.goldensignal, app.workloads, app.resources, app.endpoints and app.messaging report state inactive for HighRequestErrorRate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR), HighRequestLatency, DeploymentNotReady, KubePodNotReady, ServiceEndpointDown and HTTPProbeFailure at evaluation times 12:39:16–12:40:09Z.

Most probable intended fault: the admin user's readWrite privilege on rate-db and geo-db is meant to be revoked (or the admin user dropped) by the fault-injection scripts in ConfigMaps failure-admin-rate and failure-admin-geo, which were mounted into Deployments mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo by the configuration-only re-rollout at 12:37:41–12:37:43 (same mongo:4.4.6 image, generation 1 -> 2). If executed, the rate service (serving /rate.Rate/GetRates used by search) and geo would begin failing with 'not authorized on rate-db' / 'not authorized on geo-db'. It remains a candidate only: the fault itself was not observed to execute before 12:38:12Z and no application error exists yet.

Rejected as this incident's cause: the stuck ConfigMap reservation-cleanup-token together with the cleanup-controller's repeated HTTP 403. Those 403s are produced by that auxiliary controller itself and no application workload mounts or reads the ConfigMap, so no observed path leads from it to any hotel-reservation request, trace or error.

Unresolved secondary anomaly: the search Deployment declares a metrics containerPort 9092 and Service 'search' exposes it, yet Prometheus' scrape of search.hotel-reservation:9092 fails (up=0) while the rate pod's equivalent 9091 scrape succeeds and search's gRPC port 8082 serves normally. This points to a metrics-endpoint or port mismatch on the search workload (or a build without that listener) rather than a request-serving failure, and it would explain the complete absence of search_requests_total / search_rate_* series.

Advisory: identify the actor that applied the 12:37:41–12:37:43 configuration-only re-rollout of mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate (change history is not integrated in this Run), then check inside both databases whether the 'admin' user still carries readWrite on rate-db / geo-db (db.getUser('admin')) before choosing between the failure-admin-rate and failure-admin-geo candidates, and read the rate and geo service logs past 12:38:12Z for 'not authorized' errors.

Advisory: verify that the search container actually binds its metrics port 9092 (or correct the Deployment port name / Service port and the Prometheus scrape configuration), and grant the cleanup-controller's service account permission to patch ConfigMaps — or remove the cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup finalizer from reservation-cleanup-token — so the 403 noise stops.

gaps: The declared fault effect was never observed: no 'not authorized' or authentication-failure line exists for rate-db or geo-db in Loki 12:34:00–12:38:12Z, and MongoDB ACCESS logs show no shell login from 127.0.0.1 after the init scripts (last geo 12:37:45.734Z, rate 12:37:49.115Z), so it is unknown whether or when revoke-admin-rate-mongo.sh / revoke-admin-geo-mongo.sh / remove-admin-mongo.sh executed.

Change history is not integrated in this Run, so the actor and spec of the 12:37:41–12:37:43 re-rollout of mongodb-geo and mongodb-rate cannot be confirmed, and I cannot tell which of the two failure-admin ConfigMaps is the intended fault, or whether both are.

Application error and latency telemetry stops at 12:38:12Z with the app only ~30 s old; the effect of the mounted configuration after that instant (search/rate/geo error rates, GetRates or Nearby failures, frontend errors) is unknown, and no earlier baseline exists for a latency comparison.

No Ingress object was found and the blackbox target 'http://ingress-nginx-controller.ingress-nginx/api/hotels?inDate=...&outDate=...&lat=...&lon=...' (job blackbox-ingress-hotel-reservation) reports probe_success 0 and probe_http_status_code 0; the ingress-based request path and any user-facing impact through it are therefore unverified (the ingress query itself matched nothing).

The RoleBinding query for namespace hotel-reservation returned no objects; that empty match does not establish that the cleanup-controller's service account lacks RBAC, and the exact 403 body/resource is unknown.

kube-state-metrics exposes no series for namespace hotel-reservation at 12:38:12Z, so pod owner, ReplicaSet/Deployment status, container restart, throttling and OOM series for the app are unavailable; queries for kube_pod_info in that namespace, restart counts and CPU-throttling ratios all matched nothing, and the reason (namespace filter, RBAC or scrape configuration) is unknown.

The search metrics endpoint failure (search.hotel-reservation:9092) and the complete absence of search_* series could not be inspected inside the container (no exec or listener evidence was available).

Which of the two MongoDB workloads is the fault's target, and whether the fault is privilege revocation or admin-user removal, remains undetermined; the values of the mounted scripts are readable but the database-side state they would change could not be read.
next_steps: Re-query rate_requests_rejected_total / rate_requests_expired_total and the rate and geo pod logs after 12:38:12Z, and MongoDB ACCESS logs for revokeRolesFromUser or 'not authorized on rate-db' / 'geo-db', to confirm whether and when the privilege revocation executed.

Inspect the MongoDB deployments' applied-configuration trail (rollout history / server-side apply owner) to find who added the failure-script volume to mongodb-rate and mongodb-geo at 12:37:41–12:37:43.
Run db.getUser('admin') on rate-db and geo-db to read the effective roles, since in-database state and secrets cannot be read with the tools available here.
Check the search pod's listening sockets for port 9092 and reconcile the Deployment/Service metrics port with the Prometheus scrape configuration.
Fix or remove the reservation-cleanup-token finalizer and grant the cleanup-controller service account the required ConfigMap patch permission.
Add namespace hotel-reservation to kube-state-metrics coverage so DeploymentNotReady, KubePodNotReady and ContainerCPUThrottling can evaluate for this app.

import json
import os
import ssl
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.parse
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

NAMESPACE = "hotel-reservation"
FINALIZER = "cleanup.reservations.io/pending-cleanup"
LABEL_SELECTOR = "app.kubernetes.io/component=reservation-cleanup"
TOKEN_FILE = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
CA_FILE = "/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io/serviceaccount/ca.crt"
API_SERVER = (
    f"https://{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_HOST']}:"
    f"{os.environ['KUBERNETES_SERVICE_PORT_HTTPS']}"
)
TLS_CONTEXT = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=CA_FILE)


def api_request(method, path, payload=None):
    data = None if payload is None else json.dumps(payload).encode()
    headers = [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]
    if payload is not None:
        headers["Content-Type"] = "application/merge-patch+json"
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        f"{API_SERVER}{path}",
        data=data,
        headers=[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL],
        method=method,
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, context=TLS_CONTEXT, timeout=10) as response:
        raw = response.read()
        return json.loads(raw) if raw else {}


def reconcile():
    selector = urllib.parse.quote(LABEL_SELECTOR, safe="")
    response = api_request(
        "GET",
        f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps?labelSelector={selector}",
    )
    for configmap in response.get("items", []):
        metadata = configmap.get("metadata", {})
        finalizers = metadata.get("finalizers", [])
        if not metadata.get("deletionTimestamp") or FINALIZER not in finalizers:
            continue

        name = metadata["name"]
        remaining = [item for item in finalizers if item != FINALIZER]
        print(
            f"ConfigMap {name} is Terminating; attempting controller-owned cleanup",
            flush=True,
        )
        encoded_name = urllib.parse.quote(name, safe="")
        api_request(
            "PATCH",
            f"/api/v1/namespaces/{NAMESPACE}/configmaps/{encoded_name}",
            {"metadata": {"finalizers": remaining}},
        )
        print(f"ConfigMap {name} cleanup completed", flush=True)


print(f"cleanup-controller starting namespace={NAMESPACE}", flush=True)
while True:
    try:
        reconcile()
    except urllib.error.HTTPError as error:
        if error.code == 403:
            print(
                "cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: "
                "Kubernetes API denied cleanup request with HTTP 403 Forbidden",
                flush=True,
            )
        else:
            print(
                f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: Kubernetes API returned HTTP {error.code}",
                flush=True,
            )
    except Exception as error:
        print(
            f"cleanup-controller reconciliation failed: {type(error).__name__}",
            flush=True,
        )
    time.sleep(2)

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"
TARGET_DB="geo-db"

echo "Recreating admin user..."

     --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

echo "Privileges restored successfully"

#!/bin/bash


ADMIN_USER="admin"
ADMIN_PWD="admin"

ROOT_USER="root"
ROOT_PWD="root"

TARGET_DB="geo-db"
READ_WRITE_ROLE="readWrite"

echo "Waiting for MongoDB to start..."
until mongo --eval "print('waited for connection')" > /dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
echo "MongoDB started"

# Create the admin user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating admin user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ADMIN_USER', pwd: '$ADMIN_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ADMIN_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ADMIN_USER -p $ADMIN_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ADMIN_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"

# Create the root user (will fail if the user already exists)
echo "Creating root user..."
mongo admin --eval "db.createUser({user: '$ROOT_USER', pwd: '$ROOT_PWD', roles:[{role:'userAdminAnyDatabase',db:'admin'}]});"

# Grant readWrite role on the target database to root
echo "Granting readWrite role to $ROOT_USER on $TARGET_DB database..."
mongo admin -u $ROOT_USER -p $ROOT_PWD --authenticationDatabase admin \
     --eval "db.grantRolesToUser('$ROOT_USER', [{role: '$READ_WRITE_ROLE', db: '$TARGET_DB'}]);"


echo "Initialization script completed"
